title: From Hourly Rate to Annual Salary: What the Neymar Salary Tells Us About Pay Scales
description: Convert your hourly rate to annual salary using 38 hours per week. Includes casual loading, super, tax. Compare with the Neymar salary curiosity and Australian minimum wage.
salarySummary: Annual gross pay is hourly rate × 38 hours × 52 weeks, with casual loading and super paid on top.

faqs.q: How do I calculate my annual salary from an hourly rate?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then by 52 weeks. For a standard full-time role, assume 38 hours per week. For example, $30 per hour × 38 × 52 = $59,280 per year before tax and super. If you are casual, add 25% casual loading to the base rate first.

faqs.q: What is casual loading and how does it affect my pay?
faqs.a: Casual loading is an extra 25% paid on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for not receiving paid leave. The Fair Work Commission sets the national minimum wage for casuals at $33.05 per hour (base $26.44 plus 25%). Superannuation is calculated on the total ordinary earnings, which includes the casual loading.

faqs.q: How is superannuation calculated and when is it paid?
faqs.a: Superannuation is 12% of your ordinary time earnings, paid on top of your gross pay by your employer. For 2026–27, the maximum earnings base is $270,830. Super is not deducted from your pay; it is an additional contribution to your super fund. Use our [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page for more details.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the Hourly-to-Annual Conversion

Converting an hourly rate to an annual salary is straightforward: multiply the hourly rate by the number of hours worked per week, then by 52 weeks. For most full-time employees, the standard week is 38 hours, as set by the Fair Work Commission. This gives the formula:

**Annual gross ≈ hourly rate × 38 × 52**

If you work part-time or different hours, adjust the weekly hours accordingly. The result is your gross annual pay before tax, Medicare levy, and superannuation. To see your fortnightly pay, simply multiply your weekly pay by 2.

## The National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

From 1 July 2026, the national minimum wage is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours, according to the Fair Work Commission. This is the base rate for adult employees not covered by an award or agreement. Many employees are covered by modern awards, which often set higher minimum rates. You can find the correct award rate using the [pay guides](/blog) from the Fair Work Ombudsman.

## Casual Loading and Superannuation Paid on Top

Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for not receiving paid sick leave or annual leave. For the national minimum wage, this means a casual rate of $33.05 per hour. When using our [the timesheet](/), you can check a box to add the 25% casual loading to your base rate. **Never enter a rate that already includes casual loading** – the tool adds it for you.

Superannuation is paid on top of your ordinary earnings. The super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary time earnings, which includes casual loading for casual employees. For example, if your base hourly rate is $30 and you are casual, your ordinary earnings are $37.50 per hour ($30 + 25% loading). Super is then 12% of that, or $4.50 per hour, paid into your super fund. The maximum earnings base for super in 2026–27 is $270,830.

## The Neymar Salary Curiosity

You might search for "neymar salary" to see how much a top footballer earns – often reported in millions per year. While that scale is far beyond typical Australian wages, the same conversion principle applies: an hourly rate multiplied by hours worked per year. For most workers, the focus is on award rates, casual loading, and super. Our tool helps you see your own annual equivalent, whether you are on the minimum wage or a higher professional rate.

## Tax and Take-Home Pay

Once you have your gross annual salary, tax is deducted using the 2026–27 resident tax scale:

- $0 – $18,200: nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15c for each $1 over $18,200
- $45,001 – $135,000: 30c for each $1 over $45,000
- $135,001 – $190,000: 37c for each $1 over $135,000
- $190,001 and over: 45c for each $1 over $190,000

Plus a Medicare levy of 2% (with possible reductions for low incomes). For an estimate of your net pay, visit our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) page.

## Using the Timesheet and Reference Tables

Our [the timesheet](/), the home page, lets you enter your base hourly rate and optionally add casual loading. It then calculates your weekly, fortnightly, and annual gross pay, plus estimated tax and super. For detailed award rates and historical data, see our [reference tables](/data).

Remember: this is an estimate. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted.
